review_output.summary: [High] JSDoc @import with no import clause panics the parser on nil ImportClause
review_output.failure_scenario: A JS file containing `/** @import "./foo" */` (or a half-typed `/** @import */`) above a statement: parseImportTag's tryParseImportClause returns nil (parser.go:2199-2204), and reparser.go:120 calls importTag.ImportClause.Clone, dereferencing nil (ast.go:216) → nil-pointer panic in ParseSourceFile, crashing compiler/language server. Fix: guard `if importTag.ImportClause == nil { break }` like the typedef branch (or support a nil clause) and add a test.

review_output.summary: [High] Synthetic import shares children with JSDoc tag; setJSDocParents re-parents them, causing GetExternalModuleName panic
review_output.failure_scenario: `/** @import { Foo } from "./types" */ const x = 1;` — the shallow-cloned clause, ModuleSpecifier and Attributes are shared; the JSImportDeclaration is bound first, then the const host's setJSDocParents (binder.go:757, recursive SetParentInChildren) re-points them to the JSDocImportTag. getTargetOfImportSpecifier (checker.go:~13800) calls GetExternalModuleName(JSDocImportTag), whose case this PR removed → panic "Unhandled case"; namespace imports panic via getModuleSpecifierFromNode. Existing tests only place tags above functions (bound first). Fix: deep-clone clause/specifier/attributes for the synthetic node, or skip re-parenting JSDocImportTag children; add tests with @import above const/class.

review_output.summary: [Medium] UpdateImportDeclaration/Clone drop KindJSImportDeclaration, unlike the ExportAssignment precedent
review_output.failure_scenario: Any VisitEachChild/Update/Clone of a JSImportDeclaration returns a KindImportDeclaration, so it bypasses the `case KindJSImportDeclaration: node = nil` in esmodule.go/commonjsmodule.go and can be emitted as a runtime import; currently masked only because typeeraser removes the always-type-only clause first. Fix: use `newImportOrJSImportDeclaration(node.Kind, ...)` in both UpdateImportDeclaration and ImportDeclaration.Clone, as ast.go:4355/4369 do.

review_output.summary: [Medium] Nested @import no longer module-resolved and reported as misplaced import (TS1473)
review_output.failure_scenario: `function f() { /** @import { Foo } from "./types" */ let y; }` — parseListIndex (parser.go:478) splices the JSImportDeclaration into the block; collectModuleReferences only walks top-level statements and the removed JSDocImportTag branch of ForEachDynamicImportOrRequireCall was the only nested collector, so the module is never added to file.Imports; checkImportDeclaration reports TS1473 and bails; the alias is bound to the block/class scope instead of the file. Fix: hoist JSDoc imports to the SourceFile (like Strada's jsDocImports) or keep collecting nested ones and skip the grammar-context check for reparsed nodes; add tests.

review_output.summary: [Medium] False TS1363 on valid `@import Foo, { I }` and duplicate TS2857 under es2015 (baselines lock them in)
review_output.failure_scenario: checkJs users writing valid JSDoc `@import Foo, { I } from "./a"` get TS1363 which tsc does not emit (importTag16), and under module=es2015 get TS2857 alongside TS2823 because checkImportAttributes doesn't return after TS2823 (importTag15); the synthetic node's forced IsTypeOnly routes it through TS `import type` grammar checks. Fix: skip TS1363/TS2857 type-only checks for KindJSImportDeclaration (mirror Strada's checkJSDocImportTag) and regenerate so the .diff baselines disappear.

review_output.summary: [Medium] Accepted .types baselines print `default` instead of `Foo` for default-imported types
review_output.failure_scenario: importTag3/importTag16 previously matched Strada; now `@import Foo from "./a"` types print as `default` (visible in hover/quick info/error messages), and new .types.diff files silently accept the regression because JS tests auto-land in submoduleAccepted. Fix: name the alias symbol for the reparsed default import after its local name so the .diff files go away, or explicitly record it as a known gap.

review_output.summary: [Low] No IsAnyImportDeclaration/IsJSImportDeclaration predicate; IsImportDeclaration callers not audited
review_output.failure_scenario: ~30 sites hand-list both kinds and existing ast.IsImportDeclaration callers (emitresolver.go:148 now walks into JS imports, checker.go:14330, utilities.go:1492, completions.go:2279, ls/utilities.go:198) silently exclude the new kind, so future call sites are likely to miss it. Fix: add IsJSImportDeclaration/IsAnyImportDeclaration mirroring ast.go:4380-4386, use them in the || chains, and audit each IsImportDeclaration caller.

review_output.summary: [Low] New kind 348 sent over API but TS client SyntaxKind/childProperties unaware; ProtocolVersion not bumped
review_output.failure_scenario: API clients reading a JS file with @import decode kind 348 as SyntheticReferenceExpression in _packages/ast, and with no childProperties entry RemoteNode.getNamedChild throws "Expected only one child" when accessing importClause/moduleSpecifier; ProtocolVersion stays 1 (mirror already stale before this PR, packages private). Fix: sync _packages/ast syntaxKind enum and childProperties, and bump encoder.ProtocolVersion or generate the TS enum from kind.go.

review_output.summary: [Low] New KindJSImportDeclaration emit-path branches have no emit coverage
review_output.failure_scenario: Nothing verifies that a JS file with @import emits no require/import and no __importStar/__importDefault helpers or __esModule marker; no .js baseline exists for any @import test, and the harness skips allowJs emit baselines (js_emit_baseline.go:27-29), so the suggested compiler-runner test would not help. Fix: add a Go-level transformer unit test (or lift the harness allowJs emit restriction) asserting the emitted JS for @import named/namespace/default forms.

review_output.summary: [Low] JS-import arms in later transformers are dead and contradictory
review_output.failure_scenario: The type eraser always runs first and removes every reparsed @import via its type-only clause, so the new KindJSImportDeclaration arms in importelision, esnext, externalmoduleinfo (which would treat it as a real external import) and module transformers (which drop it) are unreachable and inconsistent; elision silently depends on IsTypeOnly. Fix: elide KindJSImportDeclaration explicitly in typeeraser's `return nil` arm alongside KindJSExportAssignment, and remove the dead arms.

review_output.summary: [Low] importTag.Modifiers() is always nil and IsTypeOnly=true is redundant
review_output.failure_scenario: JSDocImportTag has no ModifiersBase so importTag.Modifiers() always returns nil (misleading), and parseImportTag already builds the clause with isTypeOnly=true so reparser.go:122 is a no-op that implies a nonexistent invariant. Fix: pass `nil /*modifiers*/` or drop the parameter from NewJSImportDeclaration like NewJSExportAssignment, and delete the redundant IsTypeOnly assignment.

review_output.summary: [Low] importTag17 baseline still ignores resolution-mode on @import but reads like progress
review_output.failure_scenario: `@import { Import } from 'foo' with { 'resolution-mode': 'import' }` now yields TS2305/TS2749 instead of Strada's TS2322 because resolution-mode is not honored (pre-existing gap); the regenerated diff swaps one wrong result for another and can look like a partial fix. Fix: mark it as a known gap in the PR, or wire the resolution-mode override into resolution for KindJSImportDeclaration and re-baseline.

review_output.summary: [Nitpick] Duplicate `node = nil` cases for JSImportDeclaration and JSExportAssignment
review_output.failure_scenario: commonjsmodule.go and esmodule.go each have two separate one-line cases dropping JS-only synthetic nodes; a future JS-only kind would need another copy. Fix: merge into `case ast.KindJSImportDeclaration, ast.KindJSExportAssignment: node = nil` with a short comment in both files.

review_output.summary: [Nitpick] Stale JSDocImportTag references in comments after its handling was removed
review_output.failure_scenario: The AnyValidImportOrReExport comment still lists JSDocImportTag and binder.go:1595 keeps a bindJSDocImportTag placeholder, misdescribing which nodes carry module specifiers. Fix: replace JSDocImportTag with JSImportDeclaration in the comment and delete the stale binder placeholder.
